title: Taking Off. Henry My Neighbor
edition: First edition of 1,000 (May 2015); second edition of 1,000 (February 2017). ISBN 9789490800345 is shared by both.

description.main: A Dutch artist's book built from the photographs, collages and clay figures of a man named Henry, telling a story of a failed marriage, voyeurism and obsession.
description.extended:
Taking Off. Henry My Neighbor is a Dutch artist's book that assembles the photographs, collages and clay figures of a man named Henry into a story of a failed marriage, voyeurism and obsession.

Mariken Wessels presents the book as the edited archive of Henry, whose studio she reached through people she met while travelling in the United States. He had photographed his wife and muse, Martha, and sorted more than 5,500 black-and-white nudes into a private classification. When she saw the archive she threw it into the street and left. He cut up what survived, made collages, modelled clay figures from them, and finally disappeared into the woods. Across 330 pages of colour and black-and-white images, the reader follows his vision of her.

Wessels (b. 1963) trained as an actor before studying at the Gerrit Rietveld Academy, and works in artist's books, photography, film, sculpture and installation, often with appropriated imagery. The book, designed by Jurgen Maelfeyt and Wessels, was published by Art Paper Editions in May 2015 in an edition of 1,000, with a second edition of 1,000 in February 2017. It won the Author Book Award at Rencontres d'Arles in 2016 and was named among the Best Dutch Book Designs of 2015.
description.artist_bio: Mariken Wessels (b. 1963, the Netherlands) trained as an actor at the Amsterdam Theater School and later studied at the Gerrit Rietveld Academy. Solo shows include Fotomuseum Antwerp (2016) and Fotomuseum Den Haag (2017).

notes: Edition conflict: APE page and artist site say first edition May 2015, second edition Feb 2017 (Twelvebooks: '2015 (2017)'); one ISBN covers both, and the library copy's printing is unknown. year set to 2015 (first publication); change to 2017 if the copy is the second edition. Dimensions '24 x 33 cm' (APE; Twelvebooks says 240 x 330 mm), portrait per the cover scan, so height 33, width 24. Cover is the OpenLibrary flat front scan at 365x500 (low-res); the APE product image is a 2500x2000 angled mock-up, not used. Publisher blurb presents Henry as real; Wessels' own bio calls her practice appropriated and constructed imagery, so the description says 'presents the book as' and asserts nothing about his existence. Artist bio on marikenwessels.com uses 'her', so she/her is sourced.
